title: Chicken and Andouille Gumbo
subtitle: Louisiana Creole gumbo
excerpt: A deep, dark Creole gumbo built on a slow-cooked roux, with chicken, smoked sausage, the Holy Trinity of vegetables, and okra. Serve over white rice.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gumbo is one of the defining dishes of Louisiana Creole and Cajun cooking, with West African, French, and Native American roots. The dark roux, which requires patience and constant stirring to develop, is the foundation of the dish and gives gumbo its distinctive deep flavour.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy pot for the roux and the long simmer.

content.text: Gumbo starts with a dark roux: flour and oil or fat cooked over medium heat with constant stirring until the mixture turns the colour of dark chocolate. This takes 30 to 40 minutes and cannot be rushed. The roux provides the base flavour and colour of the whole dish. Once the roux is made, the rest comes together quickly.

Heat the oil in a large, heavy dutch oven over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly with a wooden spoon or flat whisk. Cook, stirring without stopping, for 30 to 40 minutes until the roux turns the colour of dark chocolate. If it starts to smell burnt, immediately move the pan off the heat and keep stirring.
Add the onion, celery, and green pepper to the hot roux. The mixture will sizzle and steam. Stir constantly for 5 minutes until the vegetables soften. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sausage and stir to coat. Gradually pour in the warm stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add the smoked paprika, thyme, oregano, cayenne, bay leaves, and salt.
Add the chicken pieces. Bring to a simmer, skimming any foam. Cover partially and cook for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the okra and cook for a further 15 minutes. Remove the bay leaves. Taste for salt and heat. Serve in bowls over white rice, topped with spring onions and parsley.
